note: Test FILES expected to fail today, and why this list exists.
The host suite is mostly red: 204 of 438 files cannot even load, nearly all
because they import fork capture/replay modules that lane F set aside in
attic/fork-typescript-do-not-use/ and which must be PORTED rather than
restored (docs/plans/2026-09-12-lane-f-census.md section 70).
A suite that is mostly red is not a signal. Two regressions in lane F's OWN
layer survived for hours inside that noise, because the gated runs used a
hand-picked file list rather than everything. This list turns the noise back
into a signal: `node host/test/suite-baseline.mjs` fails if any file OUTSIDE
it fails, and also if any file INSIDE it now passes without being removed --
the same both-directions ratchet docs/surface-budget.json uses, for the same
reason: an unbanked improvement silently funds the next regression.
This list should only ever SHRINK. Every entry removed is a file the cluster
port brought back.
2026-09-14, six files added, one cause: worker-main.ts imports
./fork-table-snapshot, which this lane set aside. They are not new breakage.
They were failing EARLIER and for a different reason -- there was no
rootfs.vfs in this worktree, so they never reached a kernel boot. Building
it (scripts/build-rootfs.sh) let them get far enough to hit the real
blocker, and the real blocker is lane F's own.
That is the shape to expect from provisioning: a missing artifact does not
hide a failure, it REPLACES it with an earlier one, and fixing the
provisioning makes the count look worse while making it truer. The same run
shows 291 files failing on that one import, so this is six more of the
same wall rather than six new problems.
A seventh file failed in that run and is deliberately NOT listed:
tests/package-system/local-build-wrapper.test.ts. It failed only because
this worktree sets KANDELO_SOURCE_CACHE_ROOT, which its fixture inherited
from the ambient environment while its expectation hard-coded the default.
It passes in a clean environment, so banking it would have hidden a real
future failure. The fixture was made hermetic instead.
2026-09-15, 48 files removed in one commit, one cause. worker-main's
NO-fork-instrumentation branch was calling `processForkUnwindTag()`, which
only an instrumented worker's fork module can answer, so a program that does
not fork could not START -- it failed before running an instruction. Both
import binders bind `env.__wpk_fork_unwind` only when the guest declares it,
so that branch now passes `undefined`. Census D9 calls this cause C1.
The list is now 136. What remains is grouped in census D9 with a count and a
priority each; the two largest are `fm_set_activation_imports` EINVAL and the
test files that import a set-aside module directly.
2026-09-15, 20 more removed, one cause family: a COW fork CHILD inherits this
module's statics through the memory clone. The fork-module's BSS lives in the
guest's memory at `__memory_base` and is not re-zeroed when the child
instantiates, so the child read the PARENT's KFIG/KFIT seed table, its
template-id table, and `PHASE` -- the last cloned MID-CAPTURE, so every
child-install entry answered EBUSY. Census D9 calls this C2.
2026-09-15, three more removed by REPOINTING rather than porting. They were
live tests that imported a set-aside module for a constant or a type:
`fork-unwind-transport` was 35 lines of re-exported `generated/abi` constants
plus two functions that live in `fork-guest-imports.ts` today, and
`process-table-replication` used three attic types only in `as unknown as`
casts that nothing checks against. Census D9 calls this group C3, and the
distinction that matters is: a test OF a set-aside module goes with it, a test
of something LIVE gets repointed.
2026-09-15: the first of the eight `fork-module-*` replay tests is ported off
the set-aside arena encoders. It no longer BUILDS a sealed KFMS arena in
TypeScript; a parent module interns and seals, a child reads what it sealed.
That is the shape a real fork has, and the only one that can catch a
capture/replay disagreement at all. `fork-module-capture-fixture.ts` holds the
shared machinery; seven files to go.
2026-09-15: the vfork BORROWED child install is wired for the first time. It
had NO host caller at all -- `fm_child_seed_borrowed` and
`fm_attach_borrowed_child` were unreferenced, so a borrowed child ran the COW
path, got no private prefix, and wrote into the parked parent's storage. The
module carves the prefixes now out of a region the host seeds; census D9 C4.
